subject: Commercial pacing & evaluation gating — proposed concession path
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@ceruleanhealth.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@ceruleanhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Early access MAP + pricing ask (Cerulean)

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is enthusiastic about the latency profile and model parity we saw. We discussed a short evaluation window and an explicit mutual action plan so we can confidently move to a paid deployment.

High-level ask: can Redwood support a staged commitment with a ramp and two pricing checkpoints tied to MAP gates? Our ideal path is:
- Pilot (30 days) — functional testing + integration (up to 50k tokens/day)
- Performance Gate — throughput & tail-latency targets met in staging
- Production Launch — full rollout, 3x token volume expected after month 2

To make the economics work for us, procurement is requesting: a 20% uplift credit for the first production month, a milestone-based discount schedule (3% at Performance Gate, 6% at 90-day volume target), and a 12-month minimum commitment for volume pricing stability. I've attached a draft MAP for your reference (Cerulean_MAP_draft.pdf).

Can you confirm whether the above is workable and what concessions Redwood would need in return (pricing tiers, commit terms)? We also want to lock a short exec review window — ideally signed within two weeks if the MAP aligns.

Best,
Elaine Park
Head of Data Product
Cerulean Health

---
Attachment: Cerulean_MAP_draft.pdf (PDF, 312KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@ceruleanhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-01T12:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Early access MAP + pricing ask (Cerulean)

Elaine — really appreciate the clear MAP draft, that makes this straightforward. Quick responses to the asks:

- Staged commit and gating: yes, we can structure a MAP with the three gates you propose (Pilot / Performance Gate / Production Launch). We typically tie discounts to verified throughput and quality checkpoints and can include a DocuSign-ready schedule.
- Upfront concessions: 20% credit for the first production month is a meaningful concession. To balance risk we'd ask for either (A) a 12-month minimum spend at a discounted unit rate (your procurement ask) or (B) a 6-month ramp guarantee with a front-loaded pro-rata payment.
- Discounting cadence: proposing an alternative tranche schedule — 2.5% at Performance Gate, 5% at 90-day volume attainment, and an additional 2.5% if year-to-date consumption exceeds forecast.

I've attached a first-pass commercial (redwood_proposal_v1.pdf) that maps pricing to the MAP gates and outlines an early ramp credit as a one-time invoice credit. Please review and flag any non-starters. If this looks directionally OK, I'd like to align execs and lock the two-week approval window you mentioned.

Action items:
- Elaine: confirm whether Cerulean needs the 12-month minimum or would accept a 6-month ramp guarantee.
- Procurement: confirm preferred billing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly invoicing).
- Internal (cc): please review commercial and advise on approval path.

Thanks — talk soon.

– Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: redwood_proposal_v1.pdf (PDF, 285KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-02T08:31:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Early access MAP + pricing ask — internal recommendation

Team — forwarding Cerulean's MAP + our first-pass proposal. Key points and my recommendation:

Quoted:
> "To make the economics work for us, procurement is requesting: a 20% uplift credit for the first production month, a milestone-based discount schedule (3% at Performance Gate, 6% at 90-day volume target), and a 12-month minimum commitment for volume pricing stability."

My read:
- Pilot: low risk to us — limited tokens. No discount.
- Performance Gate: we can accept 2.5% here; verification needs a perf-run with their staging dataset and our trace samples.
- Production Launch: recommend we offer a 15–20% one-time credit applied to month 1 billing, conditional on signing a 9–12 month committed spend (we should prefer 9 months for flexibility).

Concession ask from me: allow a 20% first-month credit but require the commit term and a revenue floor (e.g., $X minimum). That lets us protect unit economics while meeting their procurement ask.

Two asks from you both:
1) Marissa — can finance model a 20% credit with a 9-month commit vs. a 12-month commit and show the delta in NPV and payback (attach any assumptions).
2) Rishi — need a short compliance check: are there any policy blockers on a credit applied to the first invoice (billing/recognition)? Also flag any SLA exceptions.

If both green, I'll prepare a counter with the revised tranche schedule and commit floor. I want to keep exec review to a minimum (we can absorb a limited credit from quota if finance signs off).

Thanks — Adi

---
(Internal note: forward of redwood_proposal_v1.pdf included)

From: Elaine Park <elaine@ceruleanhealth.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@ceruleanhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-03T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Early access MAP + pricing ask (counter)

Aditya — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposal. Procurement reviewed and sent a counter with exact tranche numbers (attached: cerulean_counter.xlsx). Summary of their counter:
- Maintain requested 12-month minimum commitment for pricing tiers (they're firm on this).
- Request 20% credit for first production month (non-negotiable internally).
- Add an adoption milestone at 30 days where Cerulean can request rollback to pilot configuration if integration risks surface (we'd accept that as a gentle safety valve).

They also asked for a short carve-out: if Redwood needs more than 5 business days to verify Performance Gate metrics, Cerulean can request a time-boxed extension to avoid deployment slippage.

We'd like Redwood's counter that reflects: final commit length (9 v 12 months), the exact calendar for verification runs, and whether the 20% credit can be structured as a constrained discount vs. refundable invoice credit.

Best,
Elaine

---
Attachment: cerulean_counter.xlsx (XLSX, 42KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-04T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Recommended counter & escalation request — Cerulean MAP

Laura/Marissa — quick summary and an ask to escalate a limited credit authority.

Recap: Cerulean is insisting on a 12-month minimum plus a 20% first-month credit. Procurement frames the credit as a commercial requirement tied to internal approval. They also want an adoption rollback clause and a 5-business-day verification window.

My recommended counter (to send to Cerulean):
- Accept the 12-month minimum commit (commercially acceptable).
- Offer a 20% first-month concession but structure it as a one-time invoice credit convertible to a non-refundable discount if year-1 consumption >= 90% of forecast. If consumption < 60%, the credit recoups pro rata. (This preserves economics while meeting their ask.)
- Define verification windows strictly: Redwood will run Performance Gate verification within 3 business days of their staging data delivery; client has a single 5-business-day extension option.
- Keep the 30-day rollback clause but limit rollback to configuration-only (no additional credits).

Ask: I can send this counter if we have approval to commit up to a 20% one-time concession conditional on the convertible credit clause above. If we need sign-off for anything more aggressive (larger credit, fully refundable), please advise and I will route to Sales Leadership.

Related links: HubSpot (deal) and DocuSign template included above.

Thanks — Adi
